author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Rhode Island Board of Elections certified Aaron Guckian as the Republican nominee for governor Tuesday after reviews of three close primary contests did not change any winner, Rhode Island Current reported.

A rereading of voting-machine flash drives left Guckian’s margin over Elaine Pelino unchanged at 259 votes. Reviews also preserved Justin Roias’ Providence City Council Ward 4 victory, while a hand recount widened Juan Pichardo’s Ward 9 margin from nine votes to 11.

The board certified all Sept. 9 primary results. The 158,973 ballots cast represented just over 20% of registered voters, the highest Rhode Island state-primary participation rate in a decade, according to historical election data cited by Rhode Island Current.

Guckian advances to the Nov. 3 general election against Democratic nominee Helena Buonanno Foulkes and independent candidates Ken Block, Jay Gotra and C.D. Reynolds. Pelino has continued to question the review process but the certified result determines the Republican ballot line.
dek: State election officials certified the Sept. 9 primary after reviews of three close contests left their outcomes unchanged; turnout topped 20%.
headline: Rhode Island certifies Aaron Guckian as GOP governor nominee
